## Overview

Fix the `check-docstring-style` failure that has made pre-commit red on main, and on every PR, since #46871.

## Claims

- `benchmark_batched_moe.py`: double backticks in docstrings become single backticks, exactly as the hook rewrites them. No other change.

## Validation

```bash
pre-commit run check-docstring-style --files benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_batched_moe.py   # Failed (files modified) on main, Passed after
pre-commit run --files benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_batched_moe.py                         # all hooks pass
```

## Details

#65158 added the `check-docstring-style` hook, which rejects ``` ``code`` ``` in docstrings, and #46871 then merged a new `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_batched_moe.py` written in that style. Its own pre-commit ran before the hook existed, so it went in green and broke main's pre-commit from `0555390170` on (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/42539702240 is one PR inheriting it). This is the hook's own autofix, docstrings only.

No open PR fixes this (searched "benchmark_batched_moe", "check-docstring-style").

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Let the FP8 MoE oracle fall back when the global AITER flag can't serve the layer
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With only `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, the FP8 MoE oracle now prefers AITER and falls back when AITER can't serve the layer, instead of raising. Unblocks the MI355 Nemotron-3-Super FP8 ReplaySSM mirror in #66318.

## Claims

- `oracle/fp8.py`: only an explicit `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE` (set and enabled) forces the AITER FP8 MoE backend. The global flag leaves AITER first in the priority list and the normal auto selection decides.
- `test_moe_kernel_oracle.py`: `test_fp8_aiter_env_selection` covers the env combinations (global flag falls back, global flag still picks AITER when supported, explicit MoE flag still raises, either flag at 0 removes AITER).

## Validation

All runs on gfx950.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_kernel_oracle.py`, without the `fp8.py` change | `global-falls-back` fails, the other 4 new cases pass |
| Same file with the change, 10 runs in a loop | 10/10, 69 passed each |
| Same file after rebasing on current main | 69 passed |
| `test_unquantized_backend_selection.py`, `test_mxfp8_aiter_backend_selection.py`, `test_fp8_tp_loading.py` | 73 passed, 9 skipped |
| `tests/quantization/test_quark.py -k "moe or fp8"` | 56 passed, 3 skipped |
| `tests/quantization/test_online.py -k moe` | 69 passed, 1 failed (`test_online_lut_b_moe`: `lut_b_moe` is not supported on ROCm, unrelated) |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B `--quantization fp8`, only `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` | `Using AITER Fp8 MoE backend`, so AITER is still picked where it works |
| #66318 mirror: Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-FP8, TP2 + EP, ReplaySSM + MTP, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` | Without the change: `ValueError: Fp8 MoE backend 'AITER' does not support the deployment configuration since kernel does not support no act_and_mul MLP layer.` With it: `TRITON` is picked, GSM8K 3/3 pass (0.9348, 0.9310, 0.9287; acceptance length 4.24) |

Mirror command, from `tests/`: `pytest -s -v evals/gsm8k/test_gsm8k_correctness.py --config-list-file=<the #66318 Nemotron-3-Super config>`.

## Details

`select_fp8_moe_backend` treated the global `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` the same as an explicit AITER MoE request and returned `return_or_raise(AITER)`. Layers AITER can't serve, like the non-gated (no `act_and_mul`) MoE in Nemotron-3-Super FP8, then failed at startup and auto selection never got to Triton. Now the explicit path is only taken when `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE` is set, so `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1` and `--moe-backend aiter` still raise as before, and setting either flag to 0 still removes AITER. The unquantized oracle already falls back in this case (#56590), and the other MoE oracles have no such forced path.

Overlap: draft #60839 (open since 2026-10-09, last commit the same day, `needs-rebase`) has the same `oracle/fp8.py` hunk, together with an AITER custom all-reduce fallback and a Qwen-specific test in `test_fp8_tp_loading.py`. This PR is only the MoE oracle part, rebased on current main, with an env-selection test that fails without the fix. Happy to close either one in favour of the other.

commits.pr_title: [Sleep Mode] Remove level-2 workarounds that #66010 makes unnecessary
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Since #66010, level-2 sleep discards only the allocations whose live blocks are all parameters that the update rewrites. Every other allocation is offloaded and restored at the same address. State that is not a parameter now survives level 2 without help, so these workarounds can go:

- **LoRA (#39935).** Every weight replacement dropped all adapters and rebuilt the TP logits mapping, because level 2 left LoRA's GPU state undefined. LoRA has no parameters, so its state now survives, and this PR removes the reset and `LogitsProcessorWithLoRA.reset_sharded_to_full_mapping`. The hook that ran it stays, renamed from `reset_lora_state` to `on_target_weights_replaced`. Model Runner V2 still uses it to refresh the draft lm_head after a reload or weight transfer. It moves out of the LoRA mixin: Model Runner V2 defines it, and the standalone CPU runner gets an empty one, because its worker also calls it after a weight transfer. **Behavior change:** loaded adapters are no longer evicted when the base weights are replaced.
- **DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram (#59923).** The peer pointer tables were registered as buffers so that level 2 would restore them. They are now plain attributes, so `EngramPeerExchange` and `EngramBatch` no longer need to be `nn.Module`s, and the `object.__setattr__` workaround goes.
- **Comments.** Three comments gave level-2 sleep as the reason for a buffer (`rope_norm.py`, `routing_simulator_router.py`, compressed-tensors KV scales). They now give the real reason. The buffers stay: the IPC weight-cache loader builds the model on the meta device and materializes only parameters and buffers.

## Test Plan

GB200, nightly image with this branch's Python files overlaid. "Old rule" means main at 2ced9ceb97, the parent of #66010.

- LoRA: `test_sleep_mode.py -k lora` (`test_deep_sleep_lora`, `test_deep_sleep_lora_tp2`: level-2 sleep, wake, reload, compare outputs).
  - On this branch.
  - Negative control: old rule, with this PR's LoRA change and with LoRA state moved back into the weights pool (#62358's `runtime`-pool wrapper removed).
- Engram peer exchange: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, `--data-parallel-size 4 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --enable-expert-parallel`, Engram `dp_shared_memory=false`. These settings are what make `EngramBatch` build the peer exchange: a test-only hook logs every construction. Steps:
  - GSM8K (5-shot, 1319 questions) before sleep;
  - after `sleep(1)` + `wake_up()`;
  - after each of two `sleep(2)` + `wake_up(["weights"])` + `wake_up(["kv_cache"])` cycles, with all parameters preserved, so only non-parameter state is under test.

  This branch and main.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP4, two cycles of level-2 sleep and direct reload from disk.
- Unit tests:
  - `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker_weight_transfer.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py`;
  - `tests/lora/test_layers.py`, `test_lora_manager.py`, `test_worker.py`;
  - `test_sleep_mode.py`, `test_sleep_mode_tensor_ownership.py`.

## Test Result

**LoRA**

| | `test_deep_sleep_lora` | `test_deep_sleep_lora_tp2` |
|---|---|---|
| This PR | passed | passed |
| Negative control (old rule, LoRA in the weights pool, no reset) | passed | **failed** |

**Engram peer exchange**, DP4 (peer exchange built on all 4 ranks in both arms), GSM8K:

| | before | after L1 | after L2 #1 | after L2 #2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| This PR | 0.9098 | 0.9090 | 0.9030 | 0.9014 |
| main | 0.9030 | 0.9022 | 0.8992 | 0.9045 |

**DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP4, level 2 + direct reload:** GSM8K 0.9060 → 0.9037 → 0.9098. 0 of 160 expert tensors per rank differ from the cold start after each reload.

**Unit tests:**
- Worker: 71 passed.
- LoRA: 262 passed, 168 skipped.
- Sleep: 19 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed. The failure is `test_static_model_tensors_survive_level2_restore[fireredasr2]`, which needs `kaldi_native_fbank`, absent from the test environment.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Size the extensible KV cache from exact VRAM use, not 2 MB-rounded free memory
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On ROCm, `hipMemGetInfo` counts every allocation as at least 2 MB, so after warmup the extensible KV cache (#56492) sizes itself from free memory that looks a few GB smaller than it is. This PR adds that memory back once, at the final sizing, using amdgpu's exact VRAM count. Only unpartitioned discrete ROCm GPUs are affected.

**Root cause.** The amdgpu driver rounds each allocation up to 2 MB in the free memory it reports, on purpose (commit 1ac354beecfd, "drm/amdgpu: Pessimistic availability based on rounded up allocations"), unless the GPU's memory is kept in system memory (`apu_prefer_gtt`). Its own allocation check uses exact sizes. The many small kernel code objects loaded during warmup therefore hide a few GB. The sysfs counter `mem_info_vram_used` counts exact sizes for the whole device.

## Claims

- On an unpartitioned discrete ROCm GPU, the extensible KV cache sizes itself from exact device memory use. On Llama 3.1 8B / R9700 the KV cache went from 51,712 to 76,288 tokens, with no OOM and no failed requests (one run per config).
- The correction is never more than what is physically free and never negative. Other processes' allocations are not added back.
- Integrated GPUs, partitioned GPUs, a missing or mismatched sysfs count, and all non-ROCm platforms keep the current behaviour (no-op platform hooks).

## Validation

Unit tests (the sysfs lookup and correction arithmetic need no GPU; the GPU tests skip off ROCm):

```bash
pytest tests/utils_/test_rocm_vram_lookup.py tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py tests/v1/worker/test_rocm_device_memory.py
```

On a ROCm GPU (Radeon AI PRO R9700, gfx1201). `--optional` adds tests that allocate all but 256 MB of the corrected free memory, both as 64 MB / 2 MB torch blocks and as one `ExtensibleTensor` chunk (the `defragment=True` case):

```bash
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_rocm_device_memory.py --optional
```

Serving comparison, main vs this PR, with a fresh compile cache for each run:

```bash
vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.97

vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions --model meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 128 --ignore-eos \
  --request-rate inf --seed 0 --max-concurrency 128 --num-prompts 1280
# repeated with --max-concurrency 256 --num-prompts 2560
```

Llama 3.1 8B, TP1, Radeon AI PRO R9700 (32 GB), `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.97`. One run per config, so there is no variability figure:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| KV cache | 51,712 tokens | 76,288 tokens (+48%) |
| Output tok/s, concurrency 128 / 256 | 918.9 / 905.5 | 1,054.0 / 1,026.9 |
| Median TTFT, concurrency 128 / 256 | 3,934 / 25,195 ms | 1,084 / 17,110 ms |
| Most memory used / allowed | 24.6 / 31.1 GB | 27.8 / 31.1 GB |
| Failed requests / OOM | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

Not yet done:
- KV cache size across several starts.
- Multi-GPU, CDNA (MI300/MI355) and spec decode. I only have access to an R9700.


**Limitations.**
- `gpu_memory_utilization` now bounds exact use on unpartitioned discrete ROCm GPUs.
- Several instances on one GPU: with the extensible cache on, `request_memory` skips the startup check. An earlier instance's rounding is already in a later instance's baseline and is never added back, so a later instance gets a smaller cache, depending on start order. This doesn't cause OOM.
- KFD's page-table reserve and RAS pages are not in the exact count (about 80 MB on R9700). The 3 GB ROCm margin floor (#65418) covers them.
- Tested on R9700 (gfx1201) only. CDNA should behave the same according to the driver code, but this is unverified. In AMD CI, `tests/v1/worker` runs on `mi355_dpx` (partitioned, so it falls back), but other jobs run on `mi300_1` / `mi355_1`. I don't know whether those pools are partitioned. If they aren't, this path runs there untested, and the correction could be limited to validated GPUs.
- The V1 runner and `--no-enable-extensible-kv-cache` are unchanged.

**Not a duplicate.** I found no other open PR correcting ROCm's 2 MB-rounded free memory. #65413 (merged) corrects UMA free memory and is the fallback inside the new hook. #55828 (open) changes which memory counts as this process's own and only takes effect on NVML. No runtime overlap and either merge order works.

**Related:** #56492 (extensible KV cache), #65413 (UMA free-memory correction), #65418 (ROCm 3 GiB margin floor), #55828 (process-scoped KV sizing), #60121 (asynchronous VRAM release on ROCm).

**Note:** From my understanding, `amdsmi_get_gpu_memory_usage` reads the same `mem_info_vram_used` so `amdsmi` and `sysfs` should be the same but if it can't be read then it will ask KFD and will again use 2MB rounded values that hipMemGetInfo reports.

AI assistance was used. I have reviewed the changes.

## Overview

Bump the tensorizer pin from 2.10.1 to 2.12.1. With 2.10.1, `import tensorizer` fails on Python 3.14, and that failure stops vLLM engine init.

## Claims

- `rocm.txt`, the `tensorizer` extra in `setup.py`, `test/{cuda,rocm,xpu}.in` and `test/nightly-torch.txt`: tensorizer 2.10.1 -> 2.12.1.
- `test/{cpu,cuda,rocm,xpu}.txt` regenerated with their header commands. Only the tensorizer version and its two hashes change.

## Validation

Python 3.14 import (CPU torch, clean venvs):

| python | tensorizer | `import tensorizer` / `from tensorizer import _crypt` |
|---|---|---|
| 3.12 | 2.10.1 | ok |
| 3.12 | 2.12.1 | ok |
| 3.14 | 2.10.1 | `KeyError: 'crypto_stream_salsa20_NONCEBYTES'` |
| 3.14 | 2.12.1 | ok |

Tensorizer tests from the ROCm Model Executor step, run from `tests/` on MI350X (2 GPUs so the TP cases run instead of skipping), Python 3.12, torch 2.13.0+rocm:

```bash
pytest -v -s model_executor/model_loader/tensorizer_loader -m "(not slow_test) and (not distributed)"
pytest -v -s entrypoints/openai/completion/test_tensorizer_entrypoint.py
```

| tensorizer | runs | tensorizer_loader | entrypoint |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2.10.1 (baseline) | 1 | 21 passed | 1 passed |
| 2.12.1 | 4 | 21 passed each | 1 passed each |

On Python 3.14 with this bump applied, a ROCm `LLM()` greedy-generation smoke script passed 10/10 runs. Without the bump it fails at engine init.

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes, including all `pip-compile*` hooks and the nightly-torch sync hook, with no further edits. No model eval was run: the loader tests above cover serialize/deserialize round trips, and the bump does not change model execution.

## Details

tensorizer 2.10.1 builds its libsodium constants with a metaclass that reads `dct.pop("__annotations__", {})`. Under PEP 649, Python 3.14 passes `__annotate_func__` in the class namespace instead of `__annotations__`, so the lookup returns `{}` and `annotations[k]` raises `KeyError` at import. vLLM imports the tensorizer loader from `model_loader/__init__.py`, and `model_loader/tensorizer.py` only guards `ImportError`, so any 3.14 environment with 2.10.1 installed fails at `LLM(...)`. On ROCm that means every 3.14 install, because tensorizer is a runtime dep in `requirements/rocm.txt`. Upstream fixed this in coreweave/tensorizer#204 (reads annotations through `annotationlib`), released in 2.12.1. `requires_dist` and `requires_python` are the same in 2.10.1 and 2.12.1.

Not a duplicate: no open PR bumps tensorizer. I searched open PRs for "tensorizer", "tensorizer 2.12", "bump tensorizer" and "python 3.14 tensorizer". None of the matches touch the pin, and #65313 (Python 3.14 default) leaves it unchanged.

commits.pr_title: [DeepSeek-V4] Support sequence parallelism with pipeline parallelism for MegaMoE
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Enable model-level sequence parallelism (SP) for DeepSeek-V4 with MegaMoE, expert parallelism and TP > 1 when pipeline parallelism (PP) is enabled. SP keeps the residual stream sharded by token across TP ranks; the current PP = 1 condition disables it on multi-stage pipelines.

This builds on @ZacharyZcR's `requires_raw_input_tokens` fix in #55520, which supplies `input_ids` to later PP stages for MegaMoE startup. All results below include that fix. If #55520 has not been reviewed yet, please review it first. No other open PR enables SP for this combination.

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4 with MegaMoE, TP > 1 and PP > 1 now runs the same SP path as PP = 1.
- At PP2 × TP2, mean output throughput improves by 7.8% for decode and 12.9% for mixed batches; prefill is also higher.
- GSM8K accuracy is comparable to PP1 at both PP2 and PP4. Prompt logprobs match PP1 exactly when each TP rank holds more than 32 tokens; shorter prompts differ slightly because PP boundaries use different mHC kernels (see Details).
- PP = 1, non-MegaMoE backends and SP enabled only by DP > 1 are unchanged.

## Validation

`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` on B300, TP2 + EP + MegaMoE, FP8 KV cache, with the change from #55520 applied.

**Prompt logprobs.** Six fixed prompts via `/v1/completions` with `prompt_logprobs: 0` (412 scored positions), compared with PP1:

| Prompt length (tokens per TP rank) | PP2 | PP4 |
|---|---|---|
| 75 (38), 87 (44), 83 (42) | identical | identical |
| 62 (31), 59 (30), 52 (26) | mean \|Δ\| 0.037–0.061, max 0.49 | mean \|Δ\| 0.052–0.128, max 0.62 |

A diagnostic run forcing separate mHC kernels at every layer makes PP2 match PP1 at all 412 positions; see the explanation below.

**GSM8K** (1319 questions, 5-shot):

| Config | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| PP1 × TP2 (SP on) | 0.951 | unchanged |
| PP2 × TP2 | 0.949 (SP off) | 0.950 |
| PP4 × TP2 | 0.946 (SP off) | 0.955 |

**Throughput.** PP2 × TP2, output tokens/s from two interleaved runs per configuration:

| Workload (in/out, concurrency) | main (SP off) | This PR (SP on) |
|---|---|---|
| decode 512/512, c64 | 2561, 2468 | 2727, 2693 |
| mixed 2048/256, c64 | 1935, 1929 | 2204, 2159 |
| prefill 8192/16, c8 | 87.9, 74.8 | 112.7, 101.8 |

**Tests.** 48 passed:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_fi_moe_ep.py \
  tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py
```

Pre-commit passed:

```bash
pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/model.py \
  tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_fi_moe_ep.py
```

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --max-model-len 16384 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 64 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --block-size 256 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --pipeline-parallel-size 2

.venv/bin/python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 64

vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 512 --num-prompts 512 \
  --max-concurrency 64 --ignore-eos --seed 1

curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model": "...", "prompt": "...", "max_tokens": 1, "temperature": 0, "prompt_logprobs": 0}'
```
</details>

## Details

PP transport sends a slice of each `IntermediateTensors` entry from every TP rank and all-gathers the slices on the receiver. Each stage must therefore return full-token tensors replicated across TP ranks. This PR removes the PP restriction for MegaMoE and moves the exit `hidden_states` all-gather before the non-last-stage return. The next stage re-shards the received tensor on entry, following the pattern used by MiniMax-M3 and DeepSeek-V4.1. Auxiliary hidden states are already gathered per layer. SP enabled only by DP > 1 still requires PP = 1; this PR does not validate that path under PP.

**Short-prompt logprob differences.** Within a stage, mHC combines one layer's post operation with the next layer's pre operation. For up to 32 tokens per TP rank, it uses `_MHC_FUSED_TILELANG_KERNEL`; above that threshold, it uses a separate post kernel followed by a split-k GEMM. At a PP boundary, the exiting stage calls `mhc_post_tilelang` and the next stage calls `mhc_pre_tilelang` separately.

The fused and separate paths accumulate in different orders. With TP2 and SP, prompts of up to 64 tokens enter the fused path within a stage, while PP boundaries use the separate path. This explains the short-prompt differences in the table: forcing the separate path at every layer makes PP2 and PP1 logprobs identical across all 412 scored positions.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate, implement and validate this change. The submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation results.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Add check-docstring-style pre-commit hook and use single backticks in docstrings
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This touches ~31k lines across 1,848 files, but it should be the last docstring style sweep we need. The new `check-docstring-style` pre-commit hook fixes or rejects every reStructuredText-ism that breaks MkDocs rendering, on every Python file, so they can't build up again. These aren't only cosmetic: unresolvable `[a][b]` cross-references fail the docs build, as in #65157, and the hook now catches them at commit time instead.

## Claims

- Auto-fixes ` ``code`` ` to `` `code` `` and Python Sphinx roles (`:class:`~vllm.LLM`` and so on) to code spans of the text Sphinx displays.
- Rejects `[a][b]` that mkdocs-autorefs would read as a cross-reference, NumPy-style sections, RST directives (`.. note::`), RST hyperlinks, and code spans that start with a space or start or end at a line break (a misplaced backtick).
- Docstrings with escapes or line continuations can't be fixed in place, so RST markup in them is reported; the 21 such docstrings are now raw strings.
- Runs on all Python files (not just `vllm/`), except the hook's own source.
- Every changed file is exactly the hook's output on main, plus hand fixes for what it reports: 13 NumPy-style and 3 malformed docstrings converted to Google style, 4 `.. note::` to `!!! note`, 2 `.. code-block::` to fences, bracket sequences wrapped in backticks, and a few broken code spans. No paragraphs are rewrapped.
- `AGENTS.md` gets one line on docstring Markdown style, enforced by the hook.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Code vs `upstream/main`, string contents ignored | identical in all 1,845 changed `.py` files |
| Hook over every tracked `.py` file | no rewrites, no findings |
| New checks on the pre-fix versions of the files they caught | each flagged |
| Line-by-line review of the full diff (9 parallel reviewers) | findings fixed; rewrap dropped as the main source |

```bash
pre-commit run check-docstring-style --all-files   # Passed
pre-commit run                                     # all hooks pass (mypy skipped locally on macOS)
```

To regenerate on fresh main: `pre-commit run check-docstring-style --all-files`, then fix what it reports.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Keep same-host NIXL on NVLink with the extensible KV cache
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Since the extensible KV cache (#56492) became the default, same-host NIXL P/D silently moves KV over TCP instead of NVLink. This keeps NVLink: with an IMEX channel the cache gets a FABRIC handle, and without one it stays off for NIXL by default.

## Claims

- Per KV transfer, same-host: **9.9 s → about 24 ms**.
- With an IMEX channel, NVLink and the extensible KV cache work together.
- Nothing changes without NIXL on device memory.

## Validation

GLM-5.3-Flash 1P1D on one node, DEP4 + DEP4, 8x B200, driver 590.48.01, NIXL 1.5.2, real MTP 5, 1,319 GSM8K prompts:

| Build | KV read protocol | Avg transfer | GSM8K | GSM8K time |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| main | `software emulation`, `tcp/cilium_host` | 9.9 s | – | ~5 min |
| main, without `UCX_CUDA_COPY_DMABUF=no` | same | 205 s | – | >50 min |
| main, `--disable-extensible-kv-cache` | `zero-copy`, `cuda_ipc` | 23.4 ms | 0.9742 | 49 s |
| **This PR, no channel** | `zero-copy`, `cuda_ipc` | 23.6 ms | 0.9757 | 52 s |
| This PR, with a channel | `zero-copy`, `cuda_ipc` | 24.2 ms | 0.9750 | 49 s |

Both PR rows ran on `4904c38f42`. Under load, on the previous commit `ff4c74f38c` with no channel, a one-hour AgentX run at concurrency 256 made 24,041 transfers averaging 894 MB in 22.1 ms, with 0 failures.

The new tests fail with the rule and driver change reverted. To see the transport, run P and D on one node with `UCX_PROTO_INFO=y` and look for `remote memory read by ucp_get*(multi)` in D's log.

## Details

**Root cause.** No code chooses TCP. #56492 maps the KV cache with `cuMemCreate` + `cuMemMap`. UCX's `cuda_ipc` exports plain memory with `cuIpcGetMemHandle`, which cannot export driver-mapped memory, and uses a FABRIC handle only on memory created with one. So that memory has no `cuda_ipc` path and UCX picks the next transport without an error. Accuracy does not change, so #56492's NIXL accuracy check would not show it. This is inferred from UCX's protocol tables and library strings, and the comment on the `LMCacheMPConnector` gate; I did not read UCX's source.

**Fix.**
- `CudaVmmDriver` requests `CU_MEM_HANDLE_TYPE_FABRIC` when the device supports it and an IMEX channel opens. The attribute alone is not enough: it reads 1 with no channel.
- If `cuMemCreate` still rejects the FABRIC handle with `NOT_PERMITTED` or `NOT_SUPPORTED`, the errors `csrc/cumem_allocator.cpp` also falls back on, the driver allocates without it, warns, and stops requesting it for that device. Without this, such a device could not allocate the cache at all. (Nick Hill's commit.)
- `_resolve_extensible_kv_cache` keeps the feature off by default with NIXL on device memory and no channel, and logs that transfers that only cross hosts can opt back in. An explicit `--enable-extensible-kv-cache` is honored with a warning.

<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Migrate Gemma (v1) and StableLM to the Transformers modeling backend, deleting `gemma.py` and `stablelm.py`.

## Claims

- `GemmaForCausalLM` and `StableLmForCausalLM` run on the Transformers modeling backend with accuracy and throughput matching native.
- PaliGemma v1 keeps working, including text-only serving: its Gemma text config sets `use_bidirectional_attention`, so the backend now only picks `EncoderOnlyAttention` when the served model is not multimodal (`model_config.is_multimodal_model`).

## Validation

B200, Transformers 5.22, `main` vs this PR. Neither model is slower:

| Model | GSM8K (5-shot) | Throughput (req/s, 2 runs) |
|---|---|---|
| `google/gemma-1.1-2b-it` | 0.118 → 0.119 | 137.6, 113.4 → 148.3, 124.2 |
| `stabilityai/stablelm-3b-4e1t` | 0.091 → 0.097 | 27.6, 26.3 → 25.9, 26.1 |

```bash
vllm serve $MODEL --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6 --max-model-len 4096
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py
vllm bench throughput --model $MODEL --input-len 1024 --output-len 256 --num-prompts 1000 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6 --max-model-len 4096
```

Passing on this PR: `test_common` (Gemma, StableLM), `test_initialization` (Gemma, StableLM, PaliGemma, `GemmaForSequenceClassification`), PaliGemma multimodal `test_common`, `test_bge_reranker_v2_gemma`, `test_gptq_marlin` (Gemma), Gemma perplexity, `test_registry`, and `test_pipeline_parallel` with both models temporarily added to `TEST_MODELS`. PaliGemma `test_initialization`/`test_common` fail without the `base.py` change, and PaliGemma generates correctly with `limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 0}` and with `language_model_only=True`. `tests/models/transformers/test_backend.py` passes (`test_distributed` run separately).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Do not initialize CUDA when importing vendored FLA
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Importing the vendored FLA (`vllm/third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/utils.py`) initializes CUDA: platform detection calls `triton.runtime.driver.active.get_current_target()`, which goes through `torch.cuda.current_device()`, and the Hopper check calls `torch.cuda.get_device_name` / `get_device_capability`. For models whose layers import FLA at module level (GDN: Qwen3-Next/3.5, Olmo, Kimi GDN; Bailing linear attention; KDA), this happens in the API-server process while the engine config is built. vLLM then logs `We must use the spawn multiprocessing start method ... Reasons: CUDA is initialized` and spawns the engine core, which re-imports torch and vLLM.

This PR uses `current_platform` (NVML-based, no CUDA context) for the vendor and Hopper checks, so the engine core can be forked as by default.

## Test Plan

- Build the engine config for a Qwen3.5-style GDN model (`EngineArgs.create_engine_config()`) and check `torch.cuda.is_initialized()` afterwards.
- `vllm serve` startup on DGX Spark (GB10), same node, 3 starts after a discarded warm-up, page cache evicted, warm compile caches; check the spawn warning and greedy output.

## Test Result

- `torch.cuda.is_initialized()` after `create_engine_config()`: `True` before, `False` after.
- The forced-spawn warning disappears and torch is imported once instead of twice.
- Qwen3.8 27B NVFP4 + MTP, time to `/health` ready: 41.3 ± 1.8 s with spawn, 37.6 ± 3.3 s with fork. Greedy output identical.

Models without FLA at module level (e.g. Nemotron-H) are unaffected: they were already forked.
